questions.stem: Explain how the law of total probability can be used to calculate the probability of an event $A$ when the sample space is partitioned into events $B_1, B_2, \ldots, B_n$.
markingGuide: State the law of total probability formula: $P(A) = \sum_{i=1}^{n} P(A|B_i)P(B_i)$.
Explain that the law considers all possible ways $A$ can occur through the partition.
Mention that each $B_i$ is a mutually exclusive and exhaustive event.
questions.explanation: The law of total probability allows us to calculate $P(A)$ by considering all partitions $B_i$ of the sample space. For each partition, we calculate $P(A|B_i)P(B_i)$ and sum these products to find the total probability of $A$.
